newsitem.title: CHILE: German enclave in Chile opens doors to reporters.
newsitem.headline: German enclave in Chile opens doors to reporters.

text.p: Members of a secretive German colony in Chile held an open house evening for reporters in an effort to counter bad publicity they have been getting since police began daily inspections searching for community founder Paul Schaefer.

The Colonia Dignidad colony opened its doors to some 50 reporters posted outside its gates late on Friday night in a carefuly planned publicity event, with 200 children chanting in German and Spanish.
A warrant for Schaefer's arrest on charges of child abuse was issued in August, but he has refused to surrender to police.
As reporters entered the compound, the children displayed posters with the pictures of two minors who have accused Schaefer, the colony's founder, of sexually abusing them.
"We miss them and we want them to come back," one of the compound children said of the accusing minors as she read out a letter.

The parents of at least five boys in their early teens who attended a boarding school in the colony filed charges of sexual abuse and illegal detention of the children against Schaefer and other colony authorities.
The letter said the minors who have accused Schaefer were being manipulated by adults, and that the children in the colony 200 miles (320 km) south of Santiago wish to be left in peace.
Reporters were invited to enjoy beverages and pastries as part of a friendly reception from members of the village, where the Chilean police had held three succesive inspections.

Earlier on Friday, a helicopter with the green-and-white colours of Chile's Carabineros police force overflew Colonia Dignidad for several minutes, with investigating judge Hernan Gonzalez on board. Gonzalez issued the arrest warrant against Schaefer.
Officers on horseback inspected the periphery of the German enclave, which is set among scenic Andean foothills sheltering traditional Bavarian-style homes, tidy farms and electrified fences.
Schaefer's followers issued a letter on Wednesday saying he was not inside the sprawling settlement and would sooner commit suicide than give up.
"We are sure that the goal of this persecution is to close our hospital and the social good works that we have thanks to Dignidad," said Olalia Vera, after a Thursday night demonstration.

The colony's modern hospital is open only to people who support Colonia Dignidad, effectively buying the support of many of the local farmworkers and peasants, say Chilean journalists who have written about the colony.
Other supporters of the colony have been raising their voices in the last couple of days.
Residents, who have acquiesced at the police incursions, say Schaefer has not been seen for months in the colony and that police are wasting their time looking for him.
Schaefer, believed to be about 80, founded the colony in about 1960 after fleeing Germany where he was charged with molesting boys at an orphanage he founded.
